title: Photosynthesis
standard_text: The process of photosynthesis: the word and balanced equations; the light phase and the dark phase (Calvin cycle); the role of chlorophyll, light, carbon dioxide and water; limiting factors (light intensity, CO₂ concentration and temperature); greenhouses; investigations of photosynthesis. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 11, Life Sciences: Photosynthesis)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the equation, the light and dark phases, chlorophyll, limiting factors and investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The oxygen released comes from water.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts. In the light phase (in the grana), light energy splits water into hydrogen and oxygen; oxygen is released and energy is stored in ATP. In the dark phase (in the stroma), carbon dioxide is combined with hydrogen to form glucose.

The rate of photosynthesis is limited by whichever factor is in shortest supply: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration or temperature. Farmers use greenhouses to control these factors. Starch tests and the bubbles from pondweed are used to investigate photosynthesis.

Example

Which gas is released in photosynthesis?

It comes from water.

Answer: oxygen

Example

Light is increased but the rate stays the same. Why?

Another factor is limiting.

Answer: CO₂ or temperature is now limiting

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking the oxygen comes from CO₂.
  • Thinking the dark phase only happens at night.

faq.q: Why are leaves destarched before a starch test?
faq.a: So that any starch found must have been made during the experiment.

faq.q: Why is photosynthesis important for all life?
faq.a: It produces food (glucose) and oxygen and removes carbon dioxide from the air.

items.q: What is the role of NADP in photosynthesis?
c: it accepts electrons and protons, becoming reduced NADP
items.e: Reduced NADP is used to reduce GP.

items.q: What is PS II?

the splitting of water that releases oxygen
the enzyme that fixes CO₂ onto RuBP

items.q: Where does glycolysis take place?
items.e: Glucose is split into two pyruvate.

items.q: What is the word equation for photosynthesis?
c: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (in light, with chlorophyll)
items.e: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

items.q: What happens to glycerate 3-phosphate (GP) in the Calvin cycle?
c: it is reduced to triose phosphate using ATP and reduced NADP
items.e: Some triose phosphate makes glucose; most regenerates RuBP.

c: it is the main component of membranes
it carries energy from respiration to reactions that need it
items.e: ATP → ADP + Pi releases energy.

items.q: What is the law of limiting factors?
c: the largest factor controls the rate
the rate is limited by the factor that is nearest its minimum value
items.e: Proposed by Blackman.

What is an enzyme?

a protein that is a biological catalyst
items.e: Enzymes speed up reactions and are not used up.

items.q: Why does the rate of an enzyme reaction rise between 10 °C and 35 °C?
c: molecules have more kinetic energy, so enzyme–substrate collisions are more frequent
items.e: Above the optimum, denaturation takes over.

items.q: What is the first stable product of the Calvin (C₃) cycle?
items.e: It has three carbons.

items.q: What is a limiting factor?
c: the temperature at which an enzyme denatures
the factor that is present in excess
the factor that is in shortest supply and so controls the rate
a factor that stops a reaction for ever
items.e: Light, CO₂ and temperature limit photosynthesis.

items.e: He used an aquatic plant in light and dark.

items.q: What is the name for the splitting of water that releases oxygen?
items.e: Photolysis: the splitting of water that releases oxygen.

items.q: Where does the electron transport chain of aerobic respiration take place?
c: on the inner membrane (cristae) of the mitochondrion
items.e: Most ATP is made here.

items.q: What does a dehydrogenase activity experiment with DCPIP show?
c: the light-dependent reaction is happening, because DCPIP is reduced from blue to colourless
items.e: DCPIP accepts electrons instead of NADP.

items.q: Adding more carbon dioxide raises the rate of photosynthesis. What was the limiting factor before?
items.e: The limiting factor is the one that, when increased, increases the rate.

items.q: At high light intensity, the rate levels off. At 0,04% carbon dioxide and 25 °C, what is likely to be the limiting factor?
items.e: The limiting factor is the one that, when increased, increases the rate.
